analysis.title: Risk sentiment continues to moderate
key_insights: CACIB FX Risk Index at -0.7779 vs -0.9385 last week, reflecting further reduction in risk-seeking activity by investors.

The Risk Index is above its 100-day moving average for the first time since April this year, before the US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding was signed. Moves above trend have historically led to a sustained reduction in risk-seeking behaviour.
Investor risk appetite continues to wane as key geopolitical events come into view, despite the return of the AI trade.

The Israeli election is too close to call. A change of government would probably alter Israel's diplomatic tone more than its security doctrine. Netanyahu favours regime change in Iran, while Gadi Eisenkot has not explicitly called for the regime's downfall.
A more moderate Israeli PM could make it somewhat tougher for Trump to ramp back up aggressive military action against Iran, a key risk after the US midterm elections next Tuesday.
The AI trade has revived: Anthropic filed officially for its IPO, Meta's USD25bn share sale was five times oversubscribed, and Oracle deepened its partnership with OpenAI.
Microsoft and Meta report earnings later today, and Amazon and Intel report Thursday. CACIB expects these reports to have a significant impact on sentiment.

The FOMC decision later today is expected to be on hold (CACIB's US economist and the market). The statement rhetoric and Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference are the largest influences on rates and sentiment. A dovish hold would be positive for risk.

Other than lower gold prices, all factors contributed to the rise in the Risk Index over the past week. Higher equity volatility and defensive stocks outperforming cyclicals were the largest contributors.
Among G10 currencies, only CHF, CAD and SEK have significant positive correlations with the Risk Index. GBP, USD and NOK have significant negative correlations.
earnings_insights: Microsoft and Meta report earnings on 28 October 2026 (later today, per the report). Amazon and Intel report Thursday 29 October. CACIB says these reports will have a significant impact on sentiment.

Trump could ramp back up aggressive military action against Iran after the US midterm elections next Tuesday.

A hawkish FOMC statement or press conference from Chair Warsh would weigh on risk.

Defensive stocks outperforming cyclical stocks was the other largest contributor to the Risk Index rise.
Gold prices fell over the past week and were the only component that did not contribute to the Risk Index rise.
Risk Index moves above its trend have historically led to a sustained reduction in risk-seeking behaviour.
geopolitical: Israeli election is too close to call, with Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot as the two front runners for PM.
Possible US military action against Iran is a key risk after the US midterm elections next Tuesday.

tension_points.bull_case: The AI trade has revived after Anthropic's IPO filing, Meta's USD25bn share sale being five times oversubscribed, and Oracle's deeper OpenAI partnership. A dovish FOMC hold would also support risk.
tension_points.bear_case: The Risk Index is above its 100-day moving average for the first time since April, which has historically preceded a sustained reduction in risk-seeking. Geopolitical events (Israeli election, possible US action on Iran after the midterms) are approaching.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A dovish hold from the FOMC and strong Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and Intel earnings would support risk sentiment, as the report indicates.
